b: How does this policy vary from country to country?

runs: Political content ads

Political Content ads are permitted in the following countries: Argentina, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Israel, Japan, Mexico, Peru, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom and the United States. Kindly refer to country specific nuances for details.
Advertisements are subject to following restrictions:
Advertisers may not promote false or misleading content. This includes:
False or misleading information about how to participate in an election.
False or misleading information intended to intimidate or dissuade people from participating in an election.
False or misleading information intended to undermine public confidence in an election.
Advertisers must comply with any applicable laws regarding disclosure and content requirements. Such compliance is the sole responsibility of the advertiser.

Israel
Advertisers must comply with transparency and other requirements as required by Israeli law. Specifically, during election periods (i.e. 90 days prior to election day through election day itself):
the identity of the person/entity that ordered the election ad and their contact information must be shown within the ad,
the ad must not feature children under 15, and,

the ad must not feature the name or image of a member of the Israeli security forces who was injured or killed due to being a member of the security forces or the name or image of a victim of hostile action, without their explicit written consent (or family consent if deceased, with no family objections). Ads also must not portray the Israeli Defence Forces as affiliated with or identified with any party or candidate.
